claim: every independent set of the unit-distance graph on F_27^2 -- every set of points no two of which differ by a vector of quadrance 1 -- has at most 147 points
vertex_index: v = x*27 + y for the point (x, y) of F_27^2, with 0 <= x, y < 27
edge_rule: two points are adjacent iff their difference (dx, dy) satisfies dx^2 + dy^2 = 1 in F_27, where F_27 = F_3[t]/(t^3-t-1) and an element c_0 + c_1 t + ... is written as the integer whose base-3 digits are (c_0, c_1, ...), most significant first
symmetry: O(2,p) x swap x S3 acting on ordered pairs (u, v) of points: (u, v) -> (gu, gv) for g in the orthogonal group (the rotations by the points of the unit circle and the reflection (x, y) -> (x, -y)); (u, v) -> (v, u); (u, v) -> (-u, v - u)
produced_by: tools/fplane_cert_round.py (untrusted: a floating-point semidefinite solver proposes, exact rational arithmetic disposes); checked by tools/fplane_cert_check.py, which rebuilds the constraint system from q and the modulus alone)
